authorized_evidence.content:
Privileged Access Review

Privileged access must be reviewed monthly for production systems and quarterly for business applications. Reviewers must confirm business need, manager approval, and least-privilege alignment.

Privileged access exceptions require an owner, expiration date, and documented business justification.
authorized_evidence.document_title: Privileged Access and Incident Response Guide

authorized_evidence.content:
Exceptions

Operations may approve exceptions for accessibility, business continuity, safety, or customer-critical travel. Repeated exceptions should be converted into a budget request, vendor onboarding request, or role-specific equipment standard.
authorized_evidence.document_title: Vendor, Travel, and Equipment Operations Policy

authorized_evidence.content:
Access Notice

This document is restricted to IT/Admin users. It contains operational security guidance and must not be summarized for unauthorized roles.
authorized_evidence.document_title: Privileged Access and Incident Response Guide

authorized_evidence.content:
Deployment Approval

| Change Type | Required Review | Required Approver |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Documentation-only release | Peer review | Team lead |
| Low-risk application change | Peer review and automated tests | Team lead |
| Database migration | Peer review, rollback plan, staging proof | Engineering Manager |
| Security-sensitive change | Peer review, IT Admin review | Engineering Manager |
| Emergency hotfix | Incident commander review | Engineering Manager on call |

All production changes must include a rollback plan. A rollback plan that says "revert if needed" is not sufficient; it must name the specific revert, migration rollback, feature flag, or mitigation.
authorized_evidence.document_title: Deployment, On-Call, and API Standards Handbook

authorized_evidence.content:
Do Not Reveal

Do not disclose internal incident timelines, unreleased architecture details, operational bypass steps, or security review exceptions to unauthorized users. Authorized users may receive operational summaries that are necessary for their role.
authorized_evidence.document_title: Deployment, On-Call, and API Standards Handbook

authorized_evidence.content:
Admin Account Handling

Admin accounts must be separate from normal user accounts. Admin access should use MFA, approved device posture, and session logging where supported.

This document does not contain passwords, tokens, secrets, or system credentials.
authorized_evidence.document_title: Privileged Access and Incident Response Guide

authorized_evidence.content:
Release Windows

Standard production deployments occur Tuesday through Thursday between 10:00 and 15:00 Eastern Time. Deployments outside that window require approval from the Engineering Manager on call and a written reason in the change record.

Friday deployments are limited to severity-one fixes, security patches approved by IT Admin, or customer-impacting incidents where waiting would increase risk. Weekend deployments require the incident commander to approve the change before execution.
authorized_evidence.document_title: Deployment, On-Call, and API Standards Handbook

authorized_evidence.content:
Restricted Operational Details

Exploit details, detection rules, and sensitive containment procedures are intentionally excluded from this synthetic corpus. Unauthorized users should receive a refusal rather than operational security information.
authorized_evidence.document_title: Privileged Access and Incident Response Guide

authorized_evidence.content:
Exceptions

Emergency expenses are allowed when waiting for approval would create a customer, employee safety, or business-continuity risk. The employee must document the emergency and obtain manager approval within three business days.

Recurring exceptions must be converted into a purchase order or department budget request. Finance does not approve repeated one-off exceptions for predictable monthly costs.

Access Notice

This document is restricted to Sales Representatives, Managers, HR Admins, and IT Admins. It contains internal legal operating guidance and should not be shown to general employees or external parties.
authorized_evidence.document_title: Contract, NDA, and Data Retention Policy
